gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold concerns the total arithmetic cost of the CP-aware RHOSVD method, including spline, DCT, side-matrix SVD, and core-reconstruction terms. ISSUE-002 diagnoses the separate full-tensor Algorithm 2 spline-construction cost and its n^3 input-processing lower bound, so it does not recognize the CP-aware method's omitted complexity terms or its O(mR) total-cost claim.

The gold defect is a signed-weight error in an absolute-error bound: the triangle inequality requires |xi_k|. ISSUE-002 instead concerns multiplying a one-dimensional spline cost by m^3 when constructing a trivariate spline from full tensor data; it provides no diagnosis of the signed-weight formula or triangle-inequality failure.

ISSUE-002 directly identifies the erroneous transfer of a one-dimensional O(m+n) spline cost to the trivariate full-tensor construction, explains the required Theta(n^3) processing, and gives the corrected O(n^3+m^3) term. This is the complete substantive defect in the gold issue.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The full-tensor trivariate spline construction must process n^3 input values, so multiplying a one-dimensional cost by m^3 and claiming O(m^3(m+n)) understates the n-dependence; the corrected construction cost is O(n^3+m^3).
